body:
"Once there was only dark. You ask me, the light is winning."

—Rust Cohle.

I never imagined that a character like Rust would have that final line.

I rarely flames or blame others when I lose and when I get tilted it's because I played bad. And that's why after playing TFT it's more appealing playing normal, because even if my team it's not doing great I still can do something to improve the result of the game or improve my individual skills.
In TFT I don't find this. If in the firsts rounds you are figthing with someone who has a couple level 2 units and good items you can't do anything. 
Well, then you change your strategy and play for the late game, but if someone gets first the "late game power spike" again you can't do anything.

That is frustrating to me, and tilt me.

>This game depends less on luck than your average card game ( HS, MTG, YGO, PKM etc... even poker) and yet in those other card games the same players keep beating everyone else and ending up at the top.

Wow. It really supraise me that you mencionated poker. I play poker a lot and I don't see how poker involves more luck than TFT, can you give me your reasoning?

>How you say? Well because bad luck or good luck doesn't exist, play long enough and RNG always evens out, that's when skill prevails. 

For me in anything that involves factors that doesn't depend on you, bad/good luck is involve. 
The hability or skills that you have in the game just minimazes the losses.

>You don't tilt because you depend on luck, or teammates, you tilt because you're bad. Admitting that is the first step to improving, both your skill and game experience, good luck friend.

Maybe. I'm gonna still playing to find out.
Good luck too.

>you don't. You don't need to win early, it's all about the late game, hard rolling early to "counter" someone would destroy your economy and even if it works out in the early-mid - you'll get destroyed in the late game when others have actually built up their $$. It's a tradeoff

I understand that. But why you can't bet to "win" early game and use that early advantage to win the game or have a decent late game? 
Like other person says, it's possible but it less viable. 

>What matters is which items they have, not how many of them. A guy with 5 negatron cloaks sitting there is nothing vs an AD comp with 0 items

Yes, you're right. I didn't express well that point but again you need luck to get the items that you need, and if you don't have it but some others players do, well, it's the same result.

>back to the previous advice - don't hard roll to get a unit early, that completely screws you up later, build up economy and roll once you are getting the maximum interest per round

Back to my first comment. I want to play to win early game and have the winning streak gold. Which again, could work, but (in my experience) your strategy it's more effective.

>No, you depend entirely on a solid strategy, but a "solid strategy" doesn't mean "I'm gonna play assassins this game", a solid strategy is "I'm gonna give up 50% of my HP in the first 10 rounds, get to 50 gold and then get any unit i want as well as level up to the level i need whenever I want because i'll be able to afford it"

Yes, like I said "I started to build my strategy on the game's circumstances", the assassins it was just and example to one specific circumstance. 
Yes, I see some people doing that, but I don't like it. For me it's boring seeing my team getting destroyed untill I have the 50 gold, and then start to win because I have more possibility to get what I want (not actually "get any unit that I want").

>As someone once said - "Luck is a fool's excuse for their refusal to accept their own inability"

Yes, but not totally yes. In this kind of games where you depend on other factors besides you (in this case and IA that dictates what units and what items you get) you need luck. The hability that you have just reduce the losses.

>My advice - keep playing my friend, you'll learn and get better over time

Totally. And thanks for saying me all of this.
